verified_loci: Maximus of Tyre 18.9: Sappho's rivals as Socrates's — 'ὅ τιπερ Σωκράτει οἱ ἀντίτεχνοι, Πρόδικος καὶ Γοργίας καὶ Θρασύμαχος καὶ Πρωταγόρας, τοῦτο τῇ Σαπφοῖ Γοργὼ καὶ Ἀνδρομέδα'
why_seated: Or. 18.9, Sappho's art of love set beside Socrates's, her rivals beside his (Gorgo and Andromeda against Prodicus and Gorgias): the writer read as the lover and the lover read through the philosopher.
ruling: Lee Sharks, 2026-11-07: "i think we need a sappho reception history ea-corpora, whatever's public. translators, scholars. theres some ground work in the archive, notes towards a future reader i believe. the seating can include everything thats publicly available as well as declared absences and pointers for material behind pay- and access- and rights-walls"; and: "sappho reception history + future reader frameworks and related"; and at 12:47 EST, of the first draft: "this seems light on scholarly material related to the future reader proposition or sappho... and that is the focus of notes towards a future reader, is it not?" And at 14:42 EST: "lets expand it to include all materials well need for the reception study in one bundle"; the study is the operator's question of 14:13 EST: "im particularly interested in how sappho became a jealous woman rather than a writer, which i believe begins with lucretius".
research: The revision of Closing the Fragment (v7, a draft of 2026-11-07 for Alexanarch), whose §6 controls the January composition against the translators from Hall (1652) to Carson and whose §8 declares an exposure-checked panel; and the Sappho Future Reader framework, whose groundwork is Research Notes Towards the Future Reader (#1548: Part I the scholarly field, Part II the future reader in twelve strata), and whose reading by a signed-out ChatGPT on 2026-11-07 is seated as capture 0C3D (sappho-future-reader-framework-constitutive-materials-chatgpt-20261107). From v1.1, also the reception study of how Sappho became a jealous woman, from Lucretius's division of fr. 31 (DRN 3.152–58 and 4.1139–40) through Hermann's reading of 1816 and Welcker's answer to it.
